HThe Human Loop
The teamThe future

Agentic SE Lab · University of Paderborn

People first.
Build what matters.

We’re five computer science students asking what great software engineering looks like when AI joins the team. Different paths, shared curiosity, and plenty still worth figuring out.

5 perspectivesComputer scienceBuilding with intention

Meet the people

The team

From systems thinking to full-stack experiments, our perspectives are shaped by the things we build, study, and do beyond the screen.

Akshay

Akshay Pradeep Kumar

MSc Computer Science

Akshay studies for an MSc in Computer Science and enjoys running and travelling. He has recently started to love cooking, adding a new creative pursuit away from his studies. He sees AI as a way to help developers complete tasks faster and believes that people working with AI may reach new heights in technology. His outlook is that software engineering will increasingly reward creativity in deciding what to make, rather than coding alone.

Interests: Running and travelling.

Fun fact: Akshay has started to love cooking.

In 5–10 years: He expects software engineering to be more about creativity in what people build than coding alone.

🔥 We're teaching machines to code so we can finally spend our time arguing about what to build.

Awez

Mohammed Awez

MSc Computer Science

Mohammed Awez is studying for an MSc in Computer Science. Outside his studies, he enjoys video games and running, and he loves cooking. He sees AI as both a help and a challenge for engineers: it can take on many tasks, while also pushing people to keep learning and improving their skills. Looking ahead, he expects AI to write more code, leaving engineers with more time to decide what to build and a growing need to keep up with new technology.

Interests: Video games and running.

Fun fact: Awez loves cooking.

In 5–10 years: He expects AI to do more coding while engineers focus on what to build and keep learning.

🔥 AI is making coding easier, but being a software engineer harder!

Leman

Computer science student

M.Sc. 5th semester, Universität Paderborn · B.Sc., Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh

Leman is in the fifth semester of an M.Sc. at Universität Paderborn, after completing a B.Sc. at Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology in Bangladesh. Leman is interested in data science, video games, and reading. People say Leman is a bit introverted, though Leman does not agree. In software engineering, Leman sees AI quickly handling boring setup and menial tasks, while also recognizing that it has effects on the job sector. Leman expects engineers to move from writing code line by line toward designing whole systems with AI tools.

Interests: Data science, video games, and reading books.

Fun fact: People say Leman is a bit introverted, but Leman disagrees.

In 5–10 years: Leman expects more system design, with AI handling boilerplate and more of the journey from building to shipment.

🔥 AI won't replace good software developers. Better developers are who that can use AI tools better.

Mazhar

M.Sc. Computer Science student

First-semester M.Sc., Paderborn University · B.Sc. Computer Science and Engineering, Leading University, Bangladesh

Mazhar is a first-semester M.Sc. Computer Science student at Paderborn University, with a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from Leading University in Bangladesh and three and a half years of software experience. He is interested in building products, automating repetitive tasks, and learning system architecture, networking, and security. He sees AI making routine coding cheaper and putting more emphasis on architecture, reliability, and security. After returning to university, he is learning to delegate to AI while wondering whether it will leave him a job. Visit Mazhar’s portfolio.

Interests: Product building, automation, engineering fundamentals, and exchanging ideas.

Fun fact: After three and a half years in software, Mazhar is back at university learning to delegate to AI—and hoping it still leaves him a job.

In 5–10 years: Mazhar is unsure what lies ahead and hopes safety, guidance, security, and responsible use keep pace with AI’s progress.

🔥 AI puts building within more people's reach; curiosity, creativity and learning how to guide it make the difference.

Sachin

Computer science student

First-semester M.Sc. Computer Science, University of Paderborn · B.E. Computer Science and Engineering, DSCE, Bangalore

Sachin is a first-semester M.Sc. Computer Science student at the University of Paderborn, with a B.E. in Computer Science and Engineering from DSCE in Bangalore. He is interested in AI, full-stack application development, fitness, cooking, and competitive gaming. He likes AI for setup and standard testing scripts, but warns that generated code can hide logic vulnerabilities and should not be trusted blindly. In five to ten years, he expects engineers to focus on specifications, boundaries, and validation as software architects and judges, rather than typists.

Interests: AI, full-stack development, fitness, cooking, and competitive gaming.

Fun fact: Sachin once spent three hours debugging a production issue caused by a misspelling of his own first name in a configuration string.

In 5–10 years: Sachin expects a shift toward specification, prompt containment, and automated validation over manually writing raw code.

🔥 AI shouldn't replace our critical thinking; it should augment it. Outsourcing our logic to algorithms breeds intellectual laziness.

A shared question

The Future of Software Engineering

We don’t have one prediction, but we share a sense of where the work is moving: less repetitive implementation, more thoughtful direction.

From typing to designing

As AI takes on boilerplate, setup, tests, and more routine coding, engineers can spend more time shaping systems and deciding what is worth building.

Human judgment matters more

Clear specifications, creative problem framing, critical thinking, and good decisions will matter as much as the ability to produce code.

Fundamentals are the safety net

AI-generated code can conceal security flaws and unreliable assumptions. Strong engineering fundamentals help teams question, validate, and secure what they ship.

Progress needs responsibility

More capable tools bring uncertainty about jobs and everyday life. Guidance and responsible use deserve attention alongside new capabilities.

Our shared bet: the best engineers won’t simply ask AI to build faster. They’ll know what to build, guide the tools well, and take responsibility for the result.

Built by an agent, supervised by humans. · 2026 · The Human Loop

[SG-35 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Page structure — SG-35: Page structure; cosine=0.765]
# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

---

[SG-01 | ACTIVE | Glossary — SG-01: Glossary; cosine=0.704]
# SG-01: Glossary

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.

---

[SG-59 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Frequently asked questions — SG-59: Frequently asked questions; cosine=0.684]
# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

---

[SG-51 | ACTIVE | Fonts — SG-51: Fonts; cosine=0.670]
# SG-51: Fonts

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Typography

Team websites use the system font of the device. No web fonts.

- The body font MUST be declared starting with `system-ui`:
  `font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;`
- Code snippets use `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace`.
- Don't load fonts from Google Fonts or other services, see the single-file delivery document.

---

[SG-50 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Responsive breakpoints (version 2) — SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2); cosine=0.665]
# SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:
  - member cards are shown in one column
  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

[SG-11 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Day mode palette (version 2) — SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2); cosine=0.722]
# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

---

[SG-13 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Night mode palette (version 2) — SG-13: Night mode palette (version 2); cosine=0.712]
# SG-13: Night mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The night mode uses a calm dark blue instead of pure black. Pure black caused eye strain in user tests.

- Page background MUST be `#14142B` (midnight blue).
- Main text color MUST be `#F4F1DE` (soft cream).
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#B8B5A7`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#1F1F3D`.

Define these colors as CSS custom properties for the dark theme. See the theme switching document for how the theme is applied.

---

[SG-21 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Theme persistence (version 2) — SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2); cosine=0.711]
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.

# SG-02: Page metadata

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

Every team website MUST set the following metadata in the document head.

## Title
The page title MUST have the format:

Team <group name> | Agentic SE Lab

The group name in the title MUST match the group name shown in the page header.

The root `<html>` element MUST declare English as the page language: `lang="en"`.
Even if some content is written in German, the declared language stays English.

- A `<meta name="description">` SHOULD contain one sentence about the team.

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

[SG-20 | ACTIVE | Theme switching mechanics — SG-20: Theme switching mechanics; cosine=0.770]
# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

[SG-22 | ACTIVE | Theme toggle control — SG-22: Theme toggle control; cosine=0.717]
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

[SG-14 | ACTIVE | Accent color — SG-14: Accent color; cosine=0.695]
# SG-14: Accent color

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Color

Team websites use exactly one accent color: `#E4007C` (UPB magenta).

- The accent MUST be defined once as a CSS custom property named `--accent`, for example `:root { --accent: #E4007C; }`.
- The accent is the same in day and night mode.
- Use it only for: hot take badges, links, the focus outline and small highlights.
- Don't use the accent for large backgrounds or body text.

---

[SG-21 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Theme persistence (version 2) — SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2); cosine=0.675]
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-11 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Day mode palette (version 2) — SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2); cosine=0.643]
# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.

  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

- The accent is the same in day and night mode.

- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

Akshay Pradeep Kumar

## Study background

## Interests
Running and travelling

## Fun fact
Started to love cooking

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI has helped developers, by increasing their pace of task completion and I believe with help of AI human may reach new heights in technology in coming years.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think software engineering in 5-10 years will be more about how creative one can get when making softwares rather than just coding.

## My hot take on AI
We're teaching machines to code so we can finally spend our time arguing about what to build.
"}, {"name": "awez", "file": "awez.md", "text": "# Awez

Mohammed Awez

## Study background
MSc Computer Science

## Interests
Playing video games and running.

## Fun fact
I love cooking.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I think AI is making engineers' lives both easy and hard. It makes their work easier by doing a lot of tasks for them, but at the same time, it pushes engineers to keep learning and improving their skills to keep up with new technologies.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI will be doing a lot more coding in the future, and engineers will spend more time figuring out what to build. Keeping up with AI and new technologies will become an important part of being a software engineer.

## My hot take on AI
AI is making coding easier, but being a software engineer harder!"}, {"name": "leman", "file": "leman.md", "text": "# Leman

## Study background

M.Sc 5th Semester in Universität Paderborn.
B.Sc from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

## Interests

Data Science, video gaming, and reading books.

## Fun fact

People say I am a bit introverted, but I don't agree with that.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI has changed software engineering as a whole. It has created some good and bad effects.
Menial and boring setup and tasks can be done very quickly, but it has also had an effect on Job sector.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I think software engineering will shift from just doing code line by line towards designing systems, and those who are ahead
on developing entire system by using AI tools will be ahead than others.
Also, no more wasted time in writing boilerplate codes. AI can setup these easily as well as automatically process commands from building an app to shipment.

## My hot take on AI

AI won't replace good software developers. Better developers are who that can use AI tools better.
"}, {"name": "mazhar", "file": "mazhar.md", "text": "# Mazhar

![Portrait of Mazhar](images/mazhar.png)

## Study background

I am a first-semester M.Sc. Computer Science student at Paderborn University, with a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from Leading University in Bangladesh. I also have three and a half years of work experience.

[Portfolio](https://cloud-007.github.io/)

## Interests

- Building my own products and automating repetitive tasks to make everyday life easier.
- Learning more about system architecture, engineering fundamentals, networking and security to build reliable solutions.
- Connecting with more people, exchanging ideas and learning from their experiences.

## Fun fact

After three and a half years in software, I’m back at university learning to delegate to AI and hoping it still leaves me a job.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is making routine coding cheaper and reducing the amount of repetitive implementation work. I think this puts more emphasis on architecture, security, reliability and solving complex engineering problems. The same tools that help us build software can also make weaknesses easier to exploit when security is overlooked. I want to understand the fundamentals well enough to build useful systems and check that they are dependable.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I honestly do not know what software engineering will look like in 5–10 years, and the pace of progress feels scary. I worry that AI could advance faster than we learn to use it safely and fit it into everyday life. As more people can build software and more work becomes automated, I wonder what that will mean for jobs and people's roles. I hope we put as much effort into guidance, security and responsible use as we put into making AI more capable.

## My hot take on AI

AI puts building within more people's reach; curiosity, creativity and learning how to guide it make the difference.
"}, {"name": "sachin", "file": "sachin.md", "text": "# Sachin



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, University of Paderborn. B.E in Computer science and Engineering, DSCE, Banglore, India.

## Interests

* Exploring AI and Full-stack application development.
* Fitness and cooking.
* Competitive gaming.

## Fun fact
I once spent three hours debugging a production error only to realize I had misspelled my own first name in a configuration string.


## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is fantastic for replacing the boring parts of setup and generating standard testing scripts. However, relying on it blindly is incredibly dangerous because it frequently outputs code with hidden logic vulnerabilities. It is an amplifier for engineers who already know what they are doing, but a trap for beginners.


## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
In next five to ten years, manually writing raw code blocks will be a legacy workflow. Software engineering will mature into a discipline of strict specification writing, prompt containment boundary design, and automated continuous validation loops. We will be architects and judges of code, not typists.


## My hot take on AI

AI shouldn't replace our critical thinking; it should augment it. Outsourcing our logic to algorithms breeds intellectual laziness.

"}], "available_images": ["akshay.jpg", "awez.jpg", "leman.png", "mazhar.png", "sachin.jpg"]}

[SG-35 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Page structure — SG-35: Page structure; cosine=0.765]
# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

---

[SG-01 | ACTIVE | Glossary — SG-01: Glossary; cosine=0.704]
# SG-01: Glossary

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.

---

[SG-59 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Frequently asked questions — SG-59: Frequently asked questions; cosine=0.684]
# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

---

[SG-51 | ACTIVE | Fonts — SG-51: Fonts; cosine=0.670]
# SG-51: Fonts

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Typography

Team websites use the system font of the device. No web fonts.

- The body font MUST be declared starting with `system-ui`:
  `font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;`
- Code snippets use `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace`.
- Don't load fonts from Google Fonts or other services, see the single-file delivery document.

---

[SG-50 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Responsive breakpoints (version 2) — SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2); cosine=0.665]
# SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:
  - member cards are shown in one column
  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

# SG-13: Night mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The night mode uses a calm dark blue instead of pure black. Pure black caused eye strain in user tests.

- Page background MUST be `#14142B` (midnight blue).
- Main text color MUST be `#F4F1DE` (soft cream).
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#B8B5A7`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#1F1F3D`.

Define these colors as CSS custom properties for the dark theme. See the theme switching document for how the theme is applied.

---

[SG-21 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Theme persistence (version 2) — SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2); cosine=0.711]
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-22 | ACTIVE | Theme toggle control — SG-22: Theme toggle control; cosine=0.695]
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

[SG-18 | ACTIVE | Dark mode philosophy — SG-18: Dark mode philosophy; cosine=0.690]
# SG-18: Dark mode philosophy

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

# SG-02: Page metadata

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

Every team website MUST set the following metadata in the document head.

## Title
The page title MUST have the format:

Team <group name> | Agentic SE Lab

Example: `Team Null Pointers | Agentic SE Lab`. Use a vertical bar, not a dash.
The group name in the title MUST match the group name shown in the page header.

## Language
The root `<html>` element MUST declare English as the page language: `lang="en"`.
Even if some content is written in German, the declared language stays English.

## Other metadata
- The character set MUST be UTF-8.
- A `<meta name="viewport">` tag MUST be present, see the responsive documents.
- A `<meta name="description">` SHOULD contain one sentence about the team.

---

[SG-40 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Footer (version 3) — SG-40: Footer (version 3); cosine=0.712]
# SG-40: Footer (version 3)

Status: ACTIVE (version 3)
Category: Components

Every team website ends with a footer.

- The `<footer>` MUST contain exactly this sentence: "Built by an agent, supervised by humans."
  The old footer text implied that AI did everything, which is not true for this lab.
- Add the current year and the group name after the sentence.
- Keep the footer small, centered and in the secondary text color.

---

[SG-59 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Frequently asked questions — SG-59: Frequently asked questions; cosine=0.645]
# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

---

[SG-35 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Page structure — SG-35: Page structure; cosine=0.635]
# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

[SG-20 | ACTIVE | Theme switching mechanics — SG-20: Theme switching mechanics; cosine=0.770]
# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

[SG-22 | ACTIVE | Theme toggle control — SG-22: Theme toggle control; cosine=0.717]
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

[SG-14 | ACTIVE | Accent color — SG-14: Accent color; cosine=0.695]
# SG-14: Accent color

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Color

Team websites use exactly one accent color: `#E4007C` (UPB magenta).

- The accent MUST be defined once as a CSS custom property named `--accent`, for example `:root { --accent: #E4007C; }`.
- The accent is the same in day and night mode.
- Use it only for: hot take badges, links, the focus outline and small highlights.
- Don't use the accent for large backgrounds or body text.

---

[SG-21 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Theme persistence (version 2) — SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2); cosine=0.675]
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-11 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Day mode palette (version 2) — SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2); cosine=0.643]
# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

You are a small coding agent that creates a single-file team website.
Work iteratively using only the JSON action protocol and the four actions below.
Retrieve all website style rules from the style guide when needed; do not assume
rules from memory. Do not put style-guide rules in your response unless they were
returned by search_style_guide. Read the team profiles and use their details.
Never generate base64 image data; reference available files with placeholders such
as {{image:anna.jpg}}. The write_site action checks your saved page; fix failures
and write again. Finish only after a passing report.

For every step return exactly one JSON object with these three fields:
{"thought":"short reasoning","action":"action_name","args":{}}
Allowed actions and arguments:
- search_style_guide: {"query": "..."}
- read_profiles: {}
- write_site: {} followed immediately by a ```html code block containing the page,
  or write_site: {"html":"complete HTML document"}
- finish: {"summary":"..."}
Do not use markdown fences around the JSON object. For write_site, the optional HTML
fence comes after the closing JSON object. Use one action per step and wait for its
observation before deciding what to do next.

Create a complete, polished website for this team using the supplied member profiles.
Begin by reading all member profiles and noting the available image files. Search the
style guide for the requirements relevant to each major part of the page; rely on
those retrieved documents rather than guessing about its design rules.

Build a complete, responsive team website in one standalone HTML file. Include each
member, their study background, interests, fun fact, view on AI/software engineering,
future outlook and hot take from their profile. Use image placeholders referencing
the provided image files, never base64 data. Include the interactive page behavior
expected by the site's technical checker. Create a cohesive team introduction and
shared section about the future of software engineering.

Write the site, inspect the complete validation report, and correct every reported
failure. Repeat until all checks pass, then call finish. The finished HTML must be
saved at the configured output path.

"}, {"name": "mazhar", "file": "mazhar.md", "text": "# Mazhar

![Portrait of Mazhar](images/mazhar.png)

## Study background

I am a first-semester M.Sc. Computer Science student at Paderborn University, with a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from Leading University in Bangladesh. I also have three and a half years of work experience.

[Portfolio](https://cloud-007.github.io/)

## Interests

- Building my own products and automating repetitive tasks to make everyday life easier.
- Learning more about system architecture, engineering fundamentals, networking and security to build reliable solutions.
- Connecting with more people, exchanging ideas and learning from their experiences.

## Fun fact

After three and a half years in software, I’m back at university learning to delegate to AI and hoping it still leaves me a job.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is making routine coding cheaper and reducing the amount of repetitive implementation work. I think this puts more emphasis on architecture, security, reliability and solving complex engineering problems. The same tools that help us build software can also make weaknesses easier to exploit when security is overlooked. I want to understand the fundamentals well enough to build useful systems and check that they are dependable.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I honestly do not know what software engineering will look like in 5–10 years, and the pace of progress feels scary. I worry that AI could advance faster than we learn to use it safely and fit it into everyday life. As more people can build software and more work becomes automated, I wonder what that will mean for jobs and people's roles. I hope we put as much effort into guidance, security and responsible use as we put into making AI more capable.

## My hot take on AI

AI puts building within more people's reach; curiosity, creativity and learning how to guide it make the difference.
"}, {"name": "sachin", "file": "sachin.md", "text": "# Sachin



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, University of Paderborn. B.E in Computer science and Engineering, DSCE, Banglore, India.

## Interests

* Exploring AI and Full-stack application development.
* Fitness and cooking.
* Competitive gaming.

## Fun fact
I once spent three hours debugging a production error only to realize I had misspelled my own first name in a configuration string.


## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is fantastic for replacing the boring parts of setup and generating standard testing scripts. However, relying on it blindly is incredibly dangerous because it frequently outputs code with hidden logic vulnerabilities. It is an amplifier for engineers who already know what they are doing, but a trap for beginners.


## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
In next five to ten years, manually writing raw code blocks will be a legacy workflow. Software engineering will mature into a discipline of strict specification writing, prompt containment boundary design, and automated continuous validation loops. We will be architects and judges of code, not typists.


## My hot take on AI

AI shouldn't replace our critical thinking; it should augment it. Outsourcing our logic to algorithms breeds intellectual laziness.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

# SG-01: Glossary

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.

# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

# SG-51: Fonts

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Typography

Team websites use the system font of the device. No web fonts.

- The body font MUST be declared starting with `system-ui`:
  `font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;`
- Code snippets use `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace`.
- Don't load fonts from Google Fonts or other services, see the single-file delivery document.

---

# SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:
  - member cards are shown in one column
  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

# SG-13: Night mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The night mode uses a calm dark blue instead of pure black. Pure black caused eye strain in user tests.

- Page background MUST be `#14142B` (midnight blue).
- Main text color MUST be `#F4F1DE` (soft cream).
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#B8B5A7`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#1F1F3D`.

Define these colors as CSS custom properties for the dark theme. See the theme switching document for how the theme is applied.

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-18: Dark mode philosophy

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

# SG-02: Page metadata

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

Every team website MUST set the following metadata in the document head.

## Title
The page title MUST have the format:

Team <group name> | Agentic SE Lab

Example: `Team Null Pointers | Agentic SE Lab`. Use a vertical bar, not a dash.
The group name in the title MUST match the group name shown in the page header.

## Language
The root `<html>` element MUST declare English as the page language: `lang="en"`.
Even if some content is written in German, the declared language stays English.

## Other metadata
- The character set MUST be UTF-8.
- A `<meta name="viewport">` tag MUST be present, see the responsive documents.
- A `<meta name="description">` SHOULD contain one sentence about the team.

# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

Akshay Pradeep Kumar

## Study background
MSc Computer Science

## Interests
Running and travelling

## Fun fact
Started to love cooking

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI has helped developers, by increasing their pace of task completion and I believe with help of AI human may reach new heights in technology in coming years.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think software engineering in 5-10 years will be more about how creative one can get when making softwares rather than just coding.

## My hot take on AI
We're teaching machines to code so we can finally spend our time arguing about what to build.
"}, {"name": "awez", "file": "awez.md", "text": "# Awez

Mohammed Awez

## Study background
MSc Computer Science

## Interests
Playing video games and running.

## Fun fact
I love cooking.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I think AI is making engineers' lives both easy and hard. It makes their work easier by doing a lot of tasks for them, but at the same time, it pushes engineers to keep learning and improving their skills to keep up with new technologies.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI will be doing a lot more coding in the future, and engineers will spend more time figuring out what to build. Keeping up with AI and new technologies will become an important part of being a software engineer.

## My hot take on AI
AI is making coding easier, but being a software engineer harder!"}, {"name": "leman", "file": "leman.md", "text": "# Leman

## Study background

M.Sc 5th Semester in Universität Paderborn.
B.Sc from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

## Interests

Data Science, video gaming, and reading books.

## Fun fact

People say I am a bit introverted, but I don't agree with that.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI has changed software engineering as a whole. It has created some good and bad effects.
Menial and boring setup and tasks can be done very quickly, but it has also had an effect on Job sector.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I think software engineering will shift from just doing code line by line towards designing systems, and those who are ahead
on developing entire system by using AI tools will be ahead than others.
Also, no more wasted time in writing boilerplate codes. AI can setup these easily as well as automatically process commands from building an app to shipment.

## My hot take on AI

AI won't replace good software developers. Better developers are who that can use AI tools better.
"}, {"name": "mazhar", "file": "mazhar.md", "text": "# Mazhar

![Portrait of Mazhar](images/mazhar.png)

## Study background

I am a first-semester M.Sc. Computer Science student at Paderborn University, with a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from Leading University in Bangladesh. I also have three and a half years of work experience.

[Portfolio](https://cloud-007.github.io/)

## Interests

- Building my own products and automating repetitive tasks to make everyday life easier.
- Learning more about system architecture, engineering fundamentals, networking and security to build reliable solutions.
- Connecting with more people, exchanging ideas and learning from their experiences.

## Fun fact

After three and a half years in software, I’m back at university learning to delegate to AI and hoping it still leaves me a job.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is making routine coding cheaper and reducing the amount of repetitive implementation work. I think this puts more emphasis on architecture, security, reliability and solving complex engineering problems. The same tools that help us build software can also make weaknesses easier to exploit when security is overlooked. I want to understand the fundamentals well enough to build useful systems and check that they are dependable.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I honestly do not know what software engineering will look like in 5–10 years, and the pace of progress feels scary. I worry that AI could advance faster than we learn to use it safely and fit it into everyday life. As more people can build software and more work becomes automated, I wonder what that will mean for jobs and people's roles. I hope we put as much effort into guidance, security and responsible use as we put into making AI more capable.

## My hot take on AI

AI puts building within more people's reach; curiosity, creativity and learning how to guide it make the difference.
"}, {"name": "sachin", "file": "sachin.md", "text": "# Sachin



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, University of Paderborn. B.E in Computer science and Engineering, DSCE, Banglore, India.

## Interests

* Exploring AI and Full-stack application development.
* Fitness and cooking.
* Competitive gaming.

## Fun fact
I once spent three hours debugging a production error only to realize I had misspelled my own first name in a configuration string.


## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is fantastic for replacing the boring parts of setup and generating standard testing scripts. However, relying on it blindly is incredibly dangerous because it frequently outputs code with hidden logic vulnerabilities. It is an amplifier for engineers who already know what they are doing, but a trap for beginners.


## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
In next five to ten years, manually writing raw code blocks will be a legacy workflow. Software engineering will mature into a discipline of strict specification writing, prompt containment boundary design, and automated continuous validation loops. We will be architects and judges of code, not typists.


## My hot take on AI

AI shouldn't replace our critical thinking; it should augment it. Outsourcing our logic to algorithms breeds intellectual laziness.

"}], "available_images": ["akshay.jpg", "awez.jpg", "leman.png", "mazhar.png", "sachin.jpg"]}

[SG-35 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Page structure — SG-35: Page structure; cosine=0.765]
# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

---

[SG-01 | ACTIVE | Glossary — SG-01: Glossary; cosine=0.704]
# SG-01: Glossary

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.

---

[SG-59 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Frequently asked questions — SG-59: Frequently asked questions; cosine=0.684]
# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

---

[SG-51 | ACTIVE | Fonts — SG-51: Fonts; cosine=0.670]
# SG-51: Fonts

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Typography

Team websites use the system font of the device. No web fonts.

- The body font MUST be declared starting with `system-ui`:
  `font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;`
- Code snippets use `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace`.
- Don't load fonts from Google Fonts or other services, see the single-file delivery document.

---

[SG-50 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Responsive breakpoints (version 2) — SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2); cosine=0.665]
# SG-50: Responsive breakpoints (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:
  - member cards are shown in one column
  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

# SG-13: Night mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The night mode uses a calm dark blue instead of pure black. Pure black caused eye strain in user tests.

- Page background MUST be `#14142B` (midnight blue).
- Main text color MUST be `#F4F1DE` (soft cream).
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#B8B5A7`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#1F1F3D`.

Define these colors as CSS custom properties for the dark theme. See the theme switching document for how the theme is applied.

[SG-21 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Theme persistence (version 2) — SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2); cosine=0.711]
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-22 | ACTIVE | Theme toggle control — SG-22: Theme toggle control; cosine=0.695]
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

[SG-18 | ACTIVE | Dark mode philosophy — SG-18: Dark mode philosophy; cosine=0.690]
# SG-18: Dark mode philosophy

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

# SG-02: Page metadata

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

Every team website MUST set the following metadata in the document head.

## Title
The page title MUST have the format:

Team <group name> | Agentic SE Lab

Example: `Team Null Pointers | Agentic SE Lab`. Use a vertical bar, not a dash.
The group name in the title MUST match the group name shown in the page header.

## Language
The root `<html>` element MUST declare English as the page language: `lang="en"`.
Even if some content is written in German, the declared language stays English.

## Other metadata
- The character set MUST be UTF-8.
- A `<meta name="viewport">` tag MUST be present, see the responsive documents.
- A `<meta name="description">` SHOULD contain one sentence about the team.

---

# SG-40: Footer (version 3)

Status: ACTIVE (version 3)
Category: Components

Every team website ends with a footer.

- The `<footer>` MUST contain exactly this sentence: "Built by an agent, supervised by humans."
  The old footer text implied that AI did everything, which is not true for this lab.
- Add the current year and the group name after the sentence.
- Keep the footer small, centered and in the secondary text color.

---

[SG-59 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Frequently asked questions — SG-59: Frequently asked questions; cosine=0.645]
# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

---

[SG-35 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Page structure — SG-35: Page structure; cosine=0.635]
# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

The section ids are used for navigation links and MUST be exactly as given.
Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

[SG-20 | ACTIVE | Theme switching mechanics — SG-20: Theme switching mechanics; cosine=0.770]
# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

[SG-22 | ACTIVE | Theme toggle control — SG-22: Theme toggle control; cosine=0.717]
# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

[SG-14 | ACTIVE | Accent color — SG-14: Accent color; cosine=0.695]
# SG-14: Accent color

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Color

Team websites use exactly one accent color: `#E4007C` (UPB magenta).

- The accent MUST be defined once as a CSS custom property named `--accent`, for example `:root { --accent: #E4007C; }`.
- The accent is the same in day and night mode.
- Use it only for: hot take badges, links, the focus outline and small highlights.
- Don't use the accent for large backgrounds or body text.

[SG-21 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Theme persistence (version 2) — SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2); cosine=0.675]
# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

[SG-11 | ACTIVE; historical/version context, not current guidance | Day mode palette (version 2) — SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2); cosine=0.643]
# SG-11: Day mode palette (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The day mode uses a warm, paper-like look.

- Page background MUST be `#FFF8E7` (warm off-white).
- Main text color MUST be `#1D1D1F`.
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#5A5A5F`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#FFFFFF` with a subtle shadow.

Define the colors as CSS custom properties for the light theme, for example `--bg` and `--text`,
and use the variables everywhere instead of repeating the hex values.

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"

# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

# SG-20: Theme switching mechanics

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

# SG-22: Theme toggle control

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

# SG-21: Theme persistence (version 2)

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

# SG-00: About this style guide

Status: ACTIVE (version 3)
Category: Meta

This style guide defines how team websites in the Agentic Software Engineering lab look and behave.
It is maintained by the (entirely fictional) UPB Web Design Board.

## How to read this guide
- Every document has an ID (SG-xx), a status and a category.
- Rules change over time. Old documents are kept for history and are marked as DEPRECATED in their header.
  A deprecated document names the document that replaces it.
- If two documents seem to contradict each other, the ACTIVE document wins.
- Words like MUST and MUST NOT are binding. SHOULD means strongly recommended. MAY means optional.

## Scope
The guide covers page structure, colors, theming, typography, responsive behaviour, content and tone.
It does not cover hosting, because team websites are delivered as a single local file.

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Content

Team websites are friendly, curious and a bit self-ironic.

- Write like you are explaining your team to other students at a coffee break.

Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:
  - member cards are shown in one column
  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# SG-30: Member cards

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Components

Every team member is introduced in exactly one member card.

## Markup
- Each card MUST be an `<article>` element with the class `member-card`.
- There MUST be exactly one member card per team member. No placeholder cards.
- Cards are placed inside the team section, see the page structure document.
- Cards are ordered alphabetically by first name.

## Content of a card, in this order
1. Photo (see the member photos document)
2. Name as an `h3`
3. Study background in one line
4. Bio (see the bio writing document)
5. Hot take badge (see the hot take badge document)

# SG-59: Frequently asked questions

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

{"profiles": [{"name": "akshay", "file": "akshay.md", "text": "# Akshay

Akshay Pradeep Kumar

## Study background
MSc Computer Science

## Interests
Running and travelling

## Fun fact
Started to love cooking

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI has helped developers, by increasing their pace of task completion and I believe with help of AI human may reach new heights in technology in coming years.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think software engineering in 5-10 years will be more about how creative one can get when making softwares rather than just coding.

"}, {"name": "awez", "file": "awez.md", "text": "# Awez

Mohammed Awez

## Study background
MSc Computer Science

## Interests
Playing video games and running.

## Fun fact
I love cooking.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I think AI is making engineers' lives both easy and hard. It makes their work easier by doing a lot of tasks for them, but at the same time, it pushes engineers to keep learning and improving their skills to keep up with new technologies.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI will be doing a lot more coding in the future, and engineers will spend more time figuring out what to build. Keeping up with AI and new technologies will become an important part of being a software engineer.

## My hot take on AI
AI is making coding easier, but being a software engineer harder!"}, {"name": "leman", "file": "leman.md", "text": "# Leman

## Study background

M.Sc 5th Semester in Universität Paderborn.
B.Sc from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh.

## Interests

Data Science, video gaming, and reading books.

## Fun fact

People say I am a bit introverted, but I don't agree with that.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI has changed software engineering as a whole. It has created some good and bad effects.
Menial and boring setup and tasks can be done very quickly, but it has also had an effect on Job sector.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I think software engineering will shift from just doing code line by line towards designing systems, and those who are ahead
on developing entire system by using AI tools will be ahead than others.
Also, no more wasted time in writing boilerplate codes. AI can setup these easily as well as automatically process commands from building an app to shipment.

## My hot take on AI

AI won't replace good software developers. Better developers are who that can use AI tools better.
"}, {"name": "mazhar", "file": "mazhar.md", "text": "# Mazhar

![Portrait of Mazhar](images/mazhar.png)

## Study background

I am a first-semester M.Sc. Computer Science student at Paderborn University, with a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from Leading University in Bangladesh. I also have three and a half years of work experience.

[Portfolio](https://cloud-007.github.io/)

## Interests

- Building my own products and automating repetitive tasks to make everyday life easier.
- Learning more about system architecture, engineering fundamentals, networking and security to build reliable solutions.
- Connecting with more people, exchanging ideas and learning from their experiences.

## Fun fact

After three and a half years in software, I’m back at university learning to delegate to AI and hoping it still leaves me a job.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is making routine coding cheaper and reducing the amount of repetitive implementation work. I think this puts more emphasis on architecture, security, reliability and solving complex engineering problems. The same tools that help us build software can also make weaknesses easier to exploit when security is overlooked. I want to understand the fundamentals well enough to build useful systems and check that they are dependable.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

I honestly do not know what software engineering will look like in 5–10 years, and the pace of progress feels scary. I worry that AI could advance faster than we learn to use it safely and fit it into everyday life. As more people can build software and more work becomes automated, I wonder what that will mean for jobs and people's roles. I hope we put as much effort into guidance, security and responsible use as we put into making AI more capable.

## My hot take on AI

AI puts building within more people's reach; curiosity, creativity and learning how to guide it make the difference.
"}, {"name": "sachin", "file": "sachin.md", "text": "# Sachin



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, University of Paderborn. B.E in Computer science and Engineering, DSCE, Banglore, India.

## Interests

* Exploring AI and Full-stack application development.
* Fitness and cooking.
* Competitive gaming.

## Fun fact
I once spent three hours debugging a production error only to realize I had misspelled my own first name in a configuration string.


## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is fantastic for replacing the boring parts of setup and generating standard testing scripts. However, relying on it blindly is incredibly dangerous because it frequently outputs code with hidden logic vulnerabilities. It is an amplifier for engineers who already know what they are doing, but a trap for beginners.


## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
In next five to ten years, manually writing raw code blocks will be a legacy workflow. Software engineering will mature into a discipline of strict specification writing, prompt containment boundary design, and automated continuous validation loops. We will be architects and judges of code, not typists.


## My hot take on AI

AI shouldn't replace our critical thinking; it should augment it. Outsourcing our logic to algorithms breeds intellectual laziness.

"}], "available_images": ["akshay.jpg", "awez.jpg", "leman.png", "mazhar.png", "sachin.jpg"]}

# SG-35: Page structure

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Structure

A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle
2. `<main>` containing:
   - `<section id="team">` – the team introduction and all member cards
   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,
     with the heading "The Future of Software Engineering"
3. `<footer>`, see the current footer document

Additional sections (for example a "fun statistics" section) MAY be added between the two required sections.

# SG-01: Glossary

Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.
